summary.text: Marine life is the living species of the sea: over 242,000 had been documented by 2023, and perhaps two million more are still undescribed.
Life began in the oceans, which by volume still provide about 90% of the living space on Earth.
Sea algae and cyanobacteria make oxygen and lock away carbon through photosynthesis, enough to shape the chemistry of the atmosphere.

facts.label: Size range
facts.value: From 0.02-micrometre plankton to 33 m blue whales

facts.label: Microbes' share
facts.value: Estimated at about 70% or 90% of marine biomass

items.prompt: Add up all the space on Earth where living things can live, measured by volume. Roughly what share is ocean?
items.explain: By volume the oceans provide about 90% of Earth's living space; 71% is only the share of the surface they cover.

items.prompt: Early in Earth's history, a huge rise in oxygen changed ocean chemistry. Which living things were hit hardest?
items.explain: The Great Oxygenation Event likely caused a widespread extinction of anaerobes, organisms that live without oxygen.

items.prompt: A stretch of coastal water suddenly loses most of its dissolved oxygen. Which animals are most likely to die off in large numbers?
items.explain: Marine vertebrates such as fish need a lot of oxygen and suffer mass deaths in low-oxygen events, while invertebrates cope far better.

items.prompt: If you could weigh every living thing in the sea, which group would make up most of the total?
items.explain: Marine microorganisms are estimated to make up about 70% or about 90% of all marine biomass.

items.prompt: A low island in a warm sea sits on rock that living animals built up over a long time. Which animals most likely made it?
items.explain: Some marine organisms, such as corals, help create new land as their reef-building material accumulates.

items.prompt: Some fish hatch in rivers, grow up at sea, then swim back upriver. What does this kind of travel do for ecosystems?

options.label: It keeps rivers free of all other fish
It makes seawater less salty over time
It carries biomass and energy between regions
It stops algae from growing in the sea

items.explain: Migratory species such as anadromous fish move biomass and biological energy between different regions of Earth.
